home.metaTitle: Orqivanta · Client work, without the chasing
home.metaDescription: Projects, tasks, documents, files, client requests and approvals in one calm workspace for agencies and studios — with a portal clients understand.
home.eyebrow: For agencies and studios that work with clients
home.title: Client work, without the chasing.
home.lead: Orqivanta keeps projects, tasks, documents, files, requests and approvals in one workspace — with a quiet portal where clients send requests and sign off on the exact version you shared.
home.ctaFree: Free during the preview. No card, no trial clock.
home.demoNote: Free during the preview. Every person, client and project in the sample studio is fictional.
home.loopTitle: One thread, from brief to sign-off.
home.loopLead: Most tools hold one part of client work. Orqivanta follows a piece of work all the way through, so nothing has to be copied from one place to another.

request.title: Request
request.body: A client asks through the portal, using your intake form. Nothing arrives as a forwarded email chain.

plan.title: Plan
plan.body: Triage it, then turn it into a task or a whole project. The original request stays linked, word for word.

make.title: Make
make.body: Write in documents that autosave and keep versions. Upload files with previews and a full history.

review.title: Review
review.body: Ask for approval on a specific file or document version, from one reviewer or all of them.

report.title: Report
report.body: See progress, overdue work and approval turnaround, each with a written definition of what it counts.

approvals.title: Know exactly what was approved.
approvals.body: Every decision is pinned to the version the reviewer saw. Upload a new version and review reopens on its own, as the next round, with the earlier decisions kept beside it.
approvals.p1: Approve, request changes or reject, with a comment
approvals.p2: Any reviewer or every reviewer, chosen per approval
approvals.p3: Reminders before the due date, not after it

portal.title: A portal clients don’t need explained.
portal.body: Clients see only what you share with them, one item at a time: requests, deliverables, updates and approvals. Internal notes and other clients stay out of view, and the server enforces it.
portal.p1: Requests with a clear, dated timeline
portal.p2: “View as client” before you share anything
portal.p3: Each contact sees their own client account, nothing else

tasks.title: A board the whole team can read at a glance.
tasks.body: List and board views over the same tasks, with subtasks, checklists, blocking dependencies and a history of every change. Drag cards with a mouse, or move them with the keyboard.
tasks.p1: Saved views, filters and bulk edits
tasks.p2: Mentions, watchers and an inbox that stays quiet
tasks.p3: A stable link for every task

private.title: Private by default
private.body: Everything starts internal. Sharing with a client is a deliberate choice, made one item at a time.

server.title: Checked on the server
server.body: Every action, search result, export and download goes through one permission engine, with row-level security in PostgreSQL behind it.

conflicts.title: No silent overwrites
conflicts.body: Tasks, documents and approvals carry versions. If two people edit at once, you see the conflict instead of losing work.

access.title: Accessible by design
access.body: Built to WCAG 2.2 AA: a keyboard path for everything, visible focus, and status that never relies on colour alone.

home.closingTitle: See it with real-looking work inside.
home.closingBody: The sample studio holds six weeks of fictional projects, requests and approvals. Pick a role — producer, designer or client — and look around. Nothing you change there is permanent.
home.closingBodyNoDemo: Create a workspace, invite your team and set up your first client project in a few minutes.

product.metaDescription: Projects, tasks, documents, files, requests, approvals, notifications, search and reports — everything in Orqivanta’s first release, and what isn’t in it yet.
product.title: Everything a client project needs, and nothing it doesn’t.
product.lead: Orqivanta is one workspace for the whole delivery loop. This page lists what’s in the first release, in plain words, and what deliberately isn’t.

projects.title: Projects
projects.body: Goals, milestones, members and health updates, with progress computed from the work itself. Archive and restore without losing history.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.body: List and board views, subtasks, checklists, labels, priorities, due dates, watchers and blocked-by dependencies. Every change lands in the task’s history.

documents.title: Documents
documents.body: Rich text with collections, autosave and numbered versions. If someone else saved first, you get a conflict dialog — never a silent overwrite.

files.title: Files
files.body: Uploads with progress, retry and cancel. Versions, image and PDF previews, and private storage where every download is checked against permissions.

requests.title: Requests
requests.body: Intake forms per organization, a triage inbox, clarification threads and duplicate links. Convert a request into a task or a project with its context kept.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.body: On a file version, a document version or a milestone. Reviewers, due dates, an any-or-all rule, reminders, and a decision history per round.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body: An inbox with read state, email notifications and per-category preferences. Changes arrive live, and missed events are replayed after a reconnect.

search.title: Search
search.body: One search and a ⌘K command palette across projects, tasks, documents, requests and clients. Results respect permissions, down to previews and counts.

reports.title: Reports
reports.body: Progress, overdue work, throughput, cycle time, request response time and approval turnaround. Each chart has a table, a written definition and a CSV export.

admin.title: Settings & admin
admin.body: Members, invitations, teams, clients, request forms, labels, an audit log of administrative changes, and a full data export.

docs.title: Documents that keep their history
docs.body: Every save is a numbered version you can open and restore. Link a document to tasks, comment on it, and share it with a client when it’s ready.

keyboard.title: Made for the keyboard
keyboard.body: ⌘K jumps anywhere. Shortcuts are listed in-app with ?, and every drag-and-drop has a keyboard alternative.

languages.title: English and Russian
languages.body: Each person picks their language, time zone and date format. Light and dark themes follow your system or your choice.

live.title: Live, without the fragility
live.body: Updates stream to every open tab after they’re saved. Lose the connection and the app catches up on what you missed when it’s back.

product.laterLead: So you know what to expect: these are out of scope for now. You won’t find half-built buttons for them anywhere in the product.

later.public: Public request forms and custom domains

portal.metaDescription: A focused portal where clients send requests, approve exact versions, collect deliverables and read updates — and never see what you haven’t shared.
portal.title: Give clients a window, not the whole house.
portal.lead: The portal is a focused space for the people you work for: what you’ve shared with them, what needs their decision, and where their requests stand.

requests.title: Send requests
requests.body: Through the intake forms you design, with attachments. They follow each one from submitted to done, and answer your questions in its thread.

approve.title: Approve work
approve.body: Review the exact file or document version, then approve, request changes or reject — with a comment that stays on record.

deliverables.title: Collect deliverables
deliverables.body: Download what you’ve shared, with every version, from one place instead of a dozen email attachments.

updates.title: Read updates
updates.body: Project updates you chose to share, in order, next to the milestones you agreed on.

portal.internalBody: Visibility is set per item, never inferred from being on a project. A client contact sees only what’s been shared with their own client account, and the server checks that on every page, search and download.

internal.tasks: Tasks, estimates and who’s working on what
internal.unshared: Documents and files you haven’t shared
internal.others: Every other client, and their work

portal.previewBody: Every shared item has a “View as client” button that shows exactly what the client will see — the same page, with the same rules — so there are no surprises.
portal.joinBody: Invite a client contact by email. They set a password, sign in, and land in the portal — never in your internal workspace. Remove them and their access ends at once.

agencies.metaDescription: Orqivanta is shaped around how agencies and studios work: client requests, versioned sign-off, clear roles and reports everyone can read.
agencies.title: Made for studios that answer to clients.
agencies.lead: Agencies juggle more than tasks: briefs that change, feedback that arrives everywhere, and sign-offs that need to stand up months later. Orqivanta is built around that.

feedback.answer: Requests come through one portal, on your forms, and each has its own thread for clarifying questions.

version.answer: Decisions are pinned to the exact version reviewed, with the round number and comments beside them.

status.problem: Status meetings that could have been a page.
status.answer: Health updates, milestones and reports show where things stand, with definitions anyone can read.

access.problem: Freelancers and clients need different access.
access.answer: Project roles and client contacts see exactly what they need. Everything else stays internal until you share it.

agencies.rolesTitle: Roles that match how studios are organised.
agencies.rolesLead: Three organization roles, three project roles and a client contact. Owners and admins act as managers on every project.

owner.name: Owner
owner.can: Everything, including deleting the organization and transferring ownership.

admin.name: Admin
admin.can: Members, teams, clients, request forms and settings; acts as a manager on every project.

member.name: Member
member.can: Works in the projects they belong to, or open projects in their team.

manager.name: Manager
manager.can: Plans the project, shares items with the client and triages requests.

contributor.name: Contributor
contributor.can: Creates and edits tasks, documents and files; asks for approvals.

viewer.name: Viewer
viewer.can: Reads the project and joins the discussion.

client.name: Client contact
client.can: Sends requests and decides approvals in the portal, on shared items only.

org.title: Create your organization
org.body: Pick a name and an address. Your workspace lives at that address, and only members can open it.

template.title: Choose a starting template
template.body: Client website, brand identity or retainer — each with starter milestones and a status workflow — or start blank.

team.title: Invite your team
team.body: Send invitations with a role. Links expire after seven days and can be revoked.

client.title: Add a client
client.body: Create the client account, invite its contacts, and connect it to a project.

share.title: Share the first deliverable
share.body: Upload it, ask for approval, and watch the decision arrive in your inbox.

pricing.metaDescription: Orqivanta is free during the preview. No paid plans, no trial clock and no checkout.
pricing.title: Free while it’s in preview.
pricing.lead: Orqivanta is a preview and a portfolio project. There are no paid plans, no trial clock and no checkout. Everything in the first release is available to every workspace.
pricing.priceNote: per workspace, for as long as the preview runs

items.all: Every feature in the first release
items.portal: Client portal with requests and approvals
items.people: Your team and your clients’ contacts
items.reports: Reports with tables and CSV export
items.storage: 1 GB of file storage per organization
items.export: A full data export whenever you want one

pricing.noCard: You’ll never be asked for card details.

paid.a: There’s no plan for it today. If that ever changes, it will be announced in the changelog first, and nothing will change for existing workspaces without notice.

ready.q: Is it ready for real client work?
ready.a: It’s built to a production standard, but it’s a preview: there’s no support team, no uptime commitment and no backups you should rely on. Use it to evaluate, and keep your own copies of anything important.

export.q: Can I take my data out?
export.a: Yes. Owners and admins can export the organization’s data from settings at any time.

limits.a: Each organization has 1 GB of file storage, and a single file can be up to 25 MB. The limits keep a free preview sustainable.

tiers.q: Why aren’t there future plans and prices here?
tiers.a: Because they don’t exist. Showing nothing is more honest than inventing tiers.

changelog.metaDescription: Release notes for Orqivanta: what changed, when, and why.
changelog.title: What’s new.
changelog.lead: Release notes for every meaningful change, newest first. Dates are when a change landed in the main branch.

about.metaDescription: Why Orqivanta exists, the principles behind it, and how it’s built.
about.title: A careful tool, honestly described.
about.p1: Orqivanta started from a simple observation: agencies rarely lose time on the work itself. They lose it around the work — chasing feedback, hunting for the latest version, and rebuilding the state of a project from memory before every call.
about.p2: It’s a portfolio project, built by one developer to show what a complete, production-minded product looks like: real authentication, real multi-tenancy, permissions enforced on the server, and an interface that respects the people using it.
about.p3: There’s no company behind it, no investors and no customers to quote. The sample studio you can explore is fictional, and it says so wherever it appears.

calm.title: Calm over clever
calm.body: Quiet screens, clear words, and notifications only when something needs you.

honest.title: Honest by default
honest.body: No invented numbers, no fake customers, and no buttons that lead nowhere.

private.title: Private unless shared
private.body: Work stays internal until someone decides to share it, one item at a time.

everyone.title: Usable by everyone
everyone.body: Keyboard paths, readable contrast, reduced motion, and two languages from day one.

about.stackLead: A modular monolith in TypeScript. No microservices for their own sake, and nothing that needs a paid account to run.

pg.name: PostgreSQL 16
pg.body: Row-level security on every tenant table, full-text and fuzzy search

jobs.name: pg-boss
jobs.body: Background jobs for email, reminders and exports, with retries

sse.name: Server-Sent Events
sse.body: Live updates fed by LISTEN/NOTIFY, replayed after a reconnect

ui.name: Tailwind CSS and Radix UI
ui.body: Accessible components on shared design tokens

about.nameBody: Orqivanta is a coined word. The mark is an open orbit around a still point: work moving around something steady.

contact.metaDescription: Questions, feedback, accessibility problems or privacy requests — send a message and a person will read it.
contact.title: Get in touch.
contact.lead: Questions, feedback, an accessibility problem or a privacy request — it all lands in one inbox and is read by a person.
contact.expectBody: This is a portfolio project, so there’s no support team and no promised response time. Every message is read.
contact.storedBody: It’s stored in Orqivanta’s database and used only to reply to you. See the <link>privacy policy</link>.
contact.securityBody: Please describe it here with the topic “Privacy”, and don’t test against other people’s workspaces.
contact.name: Your name
contact.sentBody: If it needs a reply, it will go to {email}.

accessibility.metaDescription: Orqivanta’s accessibility statement: a WCAG 2.2 AA target, how it’s checked, known limitations, and how to report a problem.
accessibility.title: Accessibility statement
accessibility.lead: Orqivanta should work for everyone who uses it, including people who rely on a keyboard, a screen reader, magnification or reduced motion.
accessibility.targetBody: We aim to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA across the public site, the workspace and the client portal. This is a target, not a certification: no independent party has audited the product.

do.semantic: Semantic headings and landmarks, and a “Skip to content” link on every page.
do.keyboard: Every control works with a keyboard, including a keyboard alternative to drag-and-drop on boards.
do.focus: A visible focus outline on everything you can interact with.
do.labels: Labels, hints and errors tied to their fields, so screen readers announce them together.
do.colour: Status always shown with an icon and a word as well as a colour; colours chosen for AA contrast in light and dark themes.
do.motion: Animations turned off when your system asks for reduced motion.
do.charts: A table beside every chart in reports, with written definitions of each metric.
do.reflow: Layouts that work at 390 pixels wide and at 200% zoom without sideways scrolling.

accessibility.testBody: Pages are scanned with axe-core, an automated accessibility engine, in light and dark themes and at phone width, and walked through with the keyboard. Automated scans find only some problems, so a clean result is treated as a minimum, not proof. Testing with screen readers has been limited so far.

limits.editor: The rich-text editor’s toolbar and @mention suggestions haven’t been fully tested with screen readers.
limits.files: Previews show files as they were uploaded. We can’t add text alternatives to images or PDFs that people share.
limits.live: Live updates refresh what’s on screen, but not every change is announced to screen readers yet.
limits.ru: The Russian translation can lag behind English for newly added text.

accessibility.reportBody: If something gets in your way, tell us through the <link>contact form</link> and choose “Accessibility”. Say which page, what you were trying to do, and which browser and assistive technology you use. Accessibility problems are treated as bugs, not requests.
